bullets.title: Fed hawkish pivot: Rate hike odds hit 60-62% post-Warsh Jackson Hole remarks
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was perceived as marginally hawkish and credibility-enhancing, shifting focus from bond yields alone to broader financial conditions (equities, credit spreads) and concluding conditions are not sufficiently restrictive. Markets repriced September rate hike odds to 60-62%, with October at 86%. Multiple sources flag this as a regime shift: multiple expansion is over, earnings are the sole return driver, and 1-2 hikes are now expected through year-end.

bullets.title: Oil spikes to $91 Brent on U.S.-Iran military escalation; energy reflation back in play
bullets.body: Brent crude surged $3+ to $91.38/bbl and WTI hit $83 after U.S.-Iran strikes resumed and a supertanker was reportedly mined in the Hormuz strait. U.S. diesel crack spreads approached $100. Saudi Arabia is separately exploring $8B in emergency loans as war strains its finances. Multiple strategists are re-adding oil reflation trades (OIH, oil services) as a core long.

bullets.title: S&P futures -0.3%, Mag 7 mostly lower; VIX +5.3% to 15.19 — controlled pullback, not breakdown
bullets.body: Equity futures are modestly lower (S&P -0.26%, Nasdaq -0.21%) with Mag 7 mostly off 0.1–0.6% premarket, except NVDA +0.6%. VIX rose to 15.19, still below the 19 level that Hedgeye identifies as the threshold between consolidation and a bearish regime. Dealer gamma remains positive per Tier1 Alpha, dampening volatility. Systematic positioning at 82nd percentile means a -2.9% decline could trigger ~$163B of automatic selling.

bullets.title: JPM NFP preview: 'Goldilocks' range 30-70k; strong print = bond yield spike, weak = stagflation fear
bullets.body: JPM expects 50k August nonfarm payrolls vs. Street at 55k; prior print was -23k. Unemployment seen flat at 4.1%, AHE +0.25% MoM. Scenario analysis assigns only 30% odds to the benign 35-65k range (SPX -25bp to +50bp); a >95k print (10% odds) risks SPX -50 to -125bp on higher yields. 'Good news is bad news' regime firmly in place post-Jackson Hole.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro nowcast: inflation reaccelerating to 3.5% in August; Quad 3 in Q3, Quad 2 in Q4
bullets.body: Hedgeye's August CPI nowcast accelerates +14bps MoM to 3.50% after July's 3.36% print. Q3 real GDP tracks at 2.03% YoY. The quarterly macro regime sequence is Quad 3 (Q3) → Quad 2 (Q4) → challenged 1H27 with Quad 4 probabilities of 63-78%. Iran war is cited as the primary driver of oil and yield curve moves.

bullets.title: Warsh hawkish read: broader financial conditions, not bond yields, are the Fed's new signal
bullets.body: Multiple analysts note consensus misread Warsh's Jackson Hole signal — he shifted the Fed's framework from tracking bond yields to broader financial conditions (stocks, credit spreads), concluding little restraint is evident today. This implies the Fed retains optionality to hike even if bond yields rise, and that equity market softness is a factor the Fed will now monitor more explicitly.

bullets.title: European sovereign yields surging: German 30yr hits 15-year high, French 30yr at 2008 high
bullets.body: Germany's 10-year Bund yield hit a 15-year high and the 30-year reached 3.79%, while France's 30-year hit 4.93%, highest since September 2008. U.S. Treasury yields are modestly lower, creating a rare transatlantic divergence. Rising global long-end yields tighten financial conditions and reinforce the 'no multiple expansion' thesis.

bullets.title: DRAM prices +24% Q/Q in August; memory supply constrained through 2028 with multi-year LTAs locking 50-70% of capacity
bullets.body: August DRAM contract pricing rose 2.2% MoM and 24% Q/Q; NAND was flat MoM but +5.4% Q/Q. Samsung has locked ~70% of memory production through 2031 via LTAs with NVDA, MSFT, and GOOGL. HBM demand is outpacing supply by 50-70%, with memory now representing 68% of cloud CSP capex in 2027. Analysts note memory cost inflation is compressing NVDA gross margins from 75% toward 71-72%.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro positioning: long oil, gold, uranium, MSFT, AAPL, AMZN; bearish META, GOOGL, TSLA, China internet
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough rotated out of the broadening trade as SPY set lower highs, reducing beta upside. Core longs: oil services (OIH), physical uranium (SRUUF), lumber, gold, silver, copper miners, HYG, healthcare, MSFT, AAPL, AMZN. Core shorts: KWEB (bearish trade/trend), utilities (XLU down 3.7% in August). VIX below 19 supports consolidation over breakdown. Bitcoin and Ethereum remain bullish trend.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing tracking 55.2 in August; Texas manufacturing strengthens, input prices rising on oil rebound
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's August ISM Manufacturing PMI nowcast finalized at 55.2 (down from 55.6 in July). Texas manufacturing strengthened with the Dallas Fed ISM-equivalent rising to 56.2 from 53.3, driven by new orders. Input prices accelerated on the oil price rebound; output prices decelerated, suggesting tariff pass-through is largely complete. Delivery times lengthened for the fourth consecutive month.

bullets.title: Labor market weakening: August NFP est ~50k vs 12-month avg 72k; temp staffing penetration stalled
bullets.body: UBS estimates August payroll additions at ~55k, below the 12-month average of ~72k. May-June payrolls were revised down ~103k. Federal employment is down 10.6% from its October 2024 peak. Temporary help staffing is down 21.6% vs. non-SA payroll growth of 5.8% since March 2022, with penetration rate stalled at 1.58%. AI is reshaping staffing via technology-enabled sourcing.

bullets.title: Goldman: AI buildout shifting from cash- to debt-funded; hyperscalers carry $3.1T off-balance-sheet AI commitments
bullets.body: Hyperscalers are carrying $3.1 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments alongside $770B on-balance-sheet debt, with Amazon and Google FCF turning negative by 2026 and Meta approaching the same. As AI capex transitions from cash-funded to debt-funded, sensitivity to 10-year yields increases. The 22V view: companies with approved data center sites and rising compute prices (CRWV, NBIS) benefit most as token consumption accelerates.

bullets.title: China-Taiwan ship swarm raises decoupling alarm; Xi-Putin meeting at SCO adds geopolitical backdrop
bullets.body: China deployed a record number of ships around Taiwan, triggering decoupling concerns on Wall Street. Separately, Xi met Putin at the SCO summit in Bishkek. These geopolitical events compound existing U.S.-Iran tensions in weighing on risk sentiment, particularly for semiconductor supply chains with Taiwan exposure.

bullets.title: G20: Bessent pushes growth agenda, confronts China's $1.2T trade surplus amid tariff and oil headwinds
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent is convening G20 finance ministers to address China's $1.2 trillion trade surplus and emphasize deregulation as a U.S. growth lever. Complicating factors include existing tariffs, U.S.-Iran tensions, and elevated energy prices. Trump has also labeled Canada one of the 'worst abusers,' signaling continued trade friction.

bullets.title: Germany August CPI +2.9% YoY; eurozone flash HICP seen at 3.3% on energy spike
bullets.body: German headline inflation edged up 0.1pp to 2.9% in August, driven by a ~2pp acceleration in energy to +10.5% YoY. Core inflation held at 2.4%. Eurozone flash HICP is expected to print at 3.3%, reinforcing the global inflation reacceleration narrative that is keeping central banks hawkish.

bullets.title: EU DSA designations: ChatGPT as Very Large Online Search Engine; Reddit and Roblox as VLOPs
bullets.body: The European Commission designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under the Digital Services Act, imposing stricter content moderation, anti-misuse, and algorithmic transparency obligations. This increases regulatory compliance costs and potential liability for these platforms.

bullets.title: Systematic equity positioning at 82nd percentile; -2.9% decline could trigger $163B of auto-selling
bullets.body: Systematic equity positioning is elevated at the 82nd percentile and now biased toward selling. A -2.9% S&P decline from current levels could trigger approximately $163B of automatic de-grossing. Momentum strategies suffered their second-worst month in ~4 decades in July (worse only than April 2009), raising the risk of further unwind pressure. Dealer positive gamma at $4.3B dampens near-term vol.

bullets.title: India GDP +7.8% in fiscal Q1, beating estimates; India capex and defense spending outlook positive
bullets.body: India's economy expanded 7.8% in fiscal Q1, beating consensus — a macro tailwind for global EM growth and a partial offset to China/Middle East risk. JPMorgan's Asia research notes India central government capex held up YTD; defense capex expected at ~17% growth in FY27 with better FY28 visibility.

bullets.title: Freight costs rising sharply: Shanghai SCFI +143% YoY, Citi warns of 2H26 retail margin pressure
bullets.body: The Shanghai Containerized Freight Index is at $3,510/TEU, up 143% YoY and accelerating ~200bps sequentially. Citi's consumer team is hosting a freight discussion highlighting rising cost pressure for consumer and retail stocks in 2H26. BofA separately warns that oil, diesel, and agricultural price surges are squeezing consumer staples margins via limited pricing power.

bullets.title: JPM shifts equities to Tactically Cautious on rate-hike repricing, September seasonality, and positioning
bullets.body: JPM's financial strategy team turned Tactically Cautious/Neutral on equities post-Jackson Hole, citing 60% September rate hike odds, elevated systematic positioning, credit spread widening risk post-Labor Day, and negative September seasonality. Momentum indices are down 21-34% from June highs, well outside the typical 10-15% correction range, suggesting momentum unwind is already underway.
